To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nasal application of 3 aromatic substances suppresses citric acid induced reflex cough in an animal model of up-regulate cough reflex.
nasal application of 3 aromatic substances (1,8-cinole, thymo, camphor) suppressed CA-induced cough in guinea pigs with up-regulated reflex.
nasal 1, 8-cineole and camphor suppressed citric acid cough, but thymol had only a trend to suppress it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficacy of nasal pre-treatment of aromatic substances on nasal symptoms and cough induced by citric-acid.
the effect of aromatic substances on nasal symptoms and cough.
the effect of nasal application of aromatic vapours on nasal symptoms and cough in guinea pigs with experimentally induced allergic rhinitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aromatic substances have a significant effect on cough in an up-regulated cough model.
nasal application of camphor, thymol or 1,8 cineole may be beneficial for the treatment of patients with allergic rhinitis and concomitant cough.
aromatic substances suppress cough in allergic animals, but not nasal symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nasal application of 10-3M of camphor or thymol suppress CA induced cough in animals.
nasal application of 0.1% thymol or 1% camphor may have a beneficial role in treatment of cough during acute phase of rhinitis.

the effect of aromatic substances is not only on sensory nerves in the nasal cavity, but also in the airways, and the effect of aromatic vapours on cough reflex is not only due to their direct action on sensory nerves in nasal mucosa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nasal application of camphor or thymol can reduce cough in patients with allergic rhinitis.
the effect on cough can be separated from nasal symptoms.
nasal application of 10-3M thymol and 10-3 camphor suppressed cough in guinea pigs with up-regulated reflex.
